title: A plugin update silently breaks every already-initialized project: settings.json bakes a version-pinned absolute plugin path and nothing re-points it
description:
Reported by the human from repeated lived experience: an existing project stops finding the plugin after an update because the address is hardcoded to an older version. Confirmed in full.

**The mechanism.** `src/claude-settings.js#writeClaudeSettings` bakes an **absolute plugin root at call time** into the consumer project's `.claude/settings.json` — the statusline command and the context-monitor hook commands. Its own header comment states why it must: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is **not expanded in project-level settings.json**, so a literal path is the only thing that works there.

The installed plugin root is **version-pinned**:

```
~/.claude/plugins/cache/hivemind-marketplace/hivemind/0.18.0/
                                                      ^^^^^^
```

So a project initialized while 0.18.0 was installed carries, forever:

```
node "C:\...\plugins\cache\hivemind-marketplace\hivemind\0.18.0\context-monitor\statusline.mjs"
```

**What happens on update.** `/plugin update` materializes the new version into a *new* directory (`.../hivemind/0.21.0/`). The old directory goes away. Every baked path in every already-initialized project now points at a directory that no longer exists.

**Why it is silent — this is the part that makes it recurring.** A statusline command that fails does not render an error; it renders nothing. A hook whose command is missing does not announce itself. The project keeps working in every visible respect while the context-monitor auto-flush and the statusline are simply gone. Nothing in the framework detects it, and the user only notices much later that something stopped happening.

**A fix already exists and nobody is told to run it.** `node bin/init.js --apply-settings` (branch 0c, `bin/init.js:993`) re-runs `writeClaudeSettings` against an existing project — deep-merge, idempotent, no wizard, works on initialized and uninitialized projects alike. It re-bakes the current path and would fully repair this.

But `commands/update.md` never mentions it. It tells the user to run `/hivemind:apply-workflows`, explains that the plugin update "does not automatically copy new files into your project", and then states: **"You do not need to re-run `/hivemind:init-project`."** So the documented post-update procedure repairs workflows and leaves the broken paths in place.

**Timing.** This fires on *every* version bump, for *every* already-initialized consumer. Cutting a new release is precisely the event that triggers it — which makes this worth landing with the release rather than after it.

**Design note for whoever takes this.** Re-baking on update is the obvious fix, but consider whether the path can avoid being version-pinned in the first place: `installed_plugins.json` records an `installPath`, and a stable indirection (or a resolver that reads the current install path at hook time) would end the whole class rather than repairing it once per release. `src/plugin-root.js` already carries a multi-source resolver with an explicit warning that "a stale `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` must not win by mere presence" — read it before choosing. Whatever is chosen, the repair must also work for a user who updates *without* reading the release notes.
acceptance_criteria: A failing spec first reproduces the break: a project whose .claude/settings.json carries a plugin path from an older version directory, where that directory no longer exists, and the statusline/hook commands therefore point at nothing. Capture the red-run output verbatim.

Detection exists and is not silent: something reports that the baked plugin path in settings.json does not resolve, rather than the statusline and hooks failing invisibly. State plainly where the signal surfaces and what a user sees.

Repair is reachable by a user who did not read the release notes. Either the path stops being version-pinned, or the re-bake happens automatically, or commands/update.md gives the exact command - decide deliberately and record why, noting that a documentation-only fix has already failed once here since --apply-settings existed the whole time and nobody was told.

If the chosen fix keeps baking an absolute path, state explicitly why the version-pinned class cannot be ended outright, given installed_plugins.json records the current installPath and src/plugin-root.js already resolves from multiple sources.

The fix is idempotent and never clobbers unrelated user content in .claude/settings.json - writeClaudeSettings's existing deep-merge and no-duplicate-hooks guarantees must survive, and a spec must prove a pre-existing unrelated hook and setting are untouched.

A sensor covers the mechanism and fails if it is removed. If the break can only be fully reproduced across a real plugin reinstall, say so and state what the sensor covers instead rather than shipping a decorative test.
commands/update.md is corrected in both parity copies byte-identical, including the currently misleading line stating that re-running init is unnecessary after an update.
npm run test:all is green; dist rebuilt and committed if bundled source changes, with dist-parity passing.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
**APPROVE** — fix round `a91e216`. FULL depth, tier `tests-after`. **0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 4 LOW**, none blocking.

**Gate:** `npm test` 93 files / 1243 passed ⬛ `test:since -- 4e5e44a~1` 14 files / 100 passed, no zero-selection marker ⬛ `tests/context-monitor-repin-fixround.spec.js` run directly (TASK-109 dynamic-import class) 13/13 ⬛ **`test:all` quiesced: 198 passed | 1 skipped (199 files), 2298 passed | 4 skipped, 0 failed** ⬛ calibration clean.

**The developer's failure attribution was verified, not accepted:** `git diff --name-only a91e216..HEAD` shows the only interim commit is TASK-210's `49a3efb`, touching `src/claude-settings.js` (+165/-24 — exactly the reported figure), `dist/init.cjs`, `hooks/hooks.json` and two new files. **Nothing touches `repin.mjs` or `update.md`.** The scaffold spec now passes 5/5 standalone. AC8 satisfied.

## HIGH-1 — both shapes confirmed by execution

Against a real tmp project, mixed fixture — statusLine + nested `SessionStart.hooks[0]` + flat `Stop[0]`, all pointing at `C:/old/0.1.0/`:

```
after: all three -> C:\Fun\hivemind\context-monitor/...
stdout: "repaired 3 stale context-monitor paths ... All context-monitor commands
         now resolve at the current install. No action needed."
```

**Legacy flat entries are not stranded** — the already-initialized population is covered. Shape is preserved, never migrated, which is the correct boundary against TASK-210.

## HIGH-2 — independence is real, with one honest caveat

Five probes planted in shapes the repair pass cannot reach; `allCurrent` caught **every one**:

| probe | repairedCount | allCurrent |
|---|---|---|
| arbitrary key (`someFutureExtension.nested.command`) | 0 | **false** |
| non-array `hooks.Stop` (object-valued) | 0 | **false** |
| doubly-nested `hooks[].hooks[].hooks[]` | 0 | **false** |
| hybrid entry (`hooks[]` *and* flat `command`) | 1 | **false** |
| unparseable path (`detectCmDir` → null) | 0 | **false** — fails *closed* |

The hybrid case is the strongest: it is the same structural-early-return class as HIGH-1 itself, and the safety net fires. **This design would have caught HIGH-1.**

**But the answer to "do they share an assumption that makes them fail together?" is yes — exactly one.** Both `repinSite` and `countStaleContextMonitorCommandsDeep` gate on `isContextMonitorCommand` (`:55-64`). They are **traversal-independent but predicate-coupled**:

```
settings = { statusLine: { command: 'node "/old/v0.18.0/context-monitor/usage.mjs"' } }
-> repairedCount = 0, allCurrent = TRUE, path still /old/v0.18.0/ -> "No action needed."
```

Not reachable today (`buildContextMonitorEntries` bakes only three commands; `usage.mjs` is a pure library, never baked). But the deep scan's own header claims it "will not find them 'current' by omission" — for this axis, it does exactly that. Cheap fix: match on a `context-monitor/` path segment rather than the four filenames.

## HIGH-3 — ran verbatim in a plain shell

`CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` confirmed empty. Step 1 resolved the install path; step 2 exit 0. **The replacement works.** The old form still fails identically, and the doc now says so explicitly before giving the working form — right call, since the broken string is findable in the wild.

**Incidental but telling:** invoking the **installed 0.18.0** copy repaired only `statusLine` and printed nothing — a live demonstration that the pre-fix code is what the human has been running all along.

## HIGH-4 — the seam is stated honestly

`repin.mjs:38-59` explicitly **retracts its own prior claim** — *"do not read the original claim as still accurate on its own — it was conditional on this script actually repairing everything, which HIGH-1 disproved"* — and states the limit plainly: *"Repairing a path that was never going to execute repairs nothing observable. That is a WRITER/shape defect, not a path-staleness defect."* TASK-210's composition note matches from the other side.

## MEDIUM sensor — verified by construction

A regression restoring statusline-only traversal fails on **three independent assertions**: both nested hook commands `.toContain(ACTUAL_CM_DIR)`, `msg.toMatch(/3 stale/)`, and `msg.toMatch(/no action needed/i)`. No longer partial.

## Carry-forward

**MEDIUM** — `isContextMonitorCommand` is the one axis on which repair and verification fail together; the header over-claims. Unreachable today.

**LOW** — a hybrid entry carrying both `hooks[]` and flat `command` repairs only the nested side (`allCurrent=false` still catches it); `src/claude-settings.js:13-31` still carries the **superseded** AC4 rationale asserting the failure "is already closed by `repin.mjs`" — that file is TASK-210's, fold the deletion there; `update.md` could add a clause that `installPath` changes every update so step 1 must be re-run rather than the expanded command saved; and `tests/context-monitor-repin-fixround.spec.js:29-31` uses a computed dynamic import (TASK-109 class), so `test:changed` selects zero specs for a `repin.mjs`-only change.

**Deferral agreed:** mixed path separators — the substring splice is the conservative algorithm and `C:\a\b/c.mjs` resolves correctly on Windows.

**Verdict: APPROVE.** All four HIGHs closed and independently verified by execution.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**CLOSED on a green independent review after one fix round.** Review depth **FULL**; rubric inputs: 294 insertions / 19 deletions in round 1 plus the fix round, and the diff touches the **plugin install/upgrade path** — a shipped surface every consumer traverses — and `src/claude-settings.js`, which feeds bundled `dist/init.cjs`.

Commits `4e5e44a` and `a91e216`. **Human-reported from repeated lived experience**, and the investigation ended somewhere quite different from where the ticket started.

## The ticket's premise was wrong, and finding that out was the valuable part

I wrote this ticket believing nothing detected or healed stale plugin paths, and that `--apply-settings` was the repair nobody was told to run. **Both were wrong, and the developer checked rather than building on my framing:**

- `context-monitor/repin.mjs` has existed since **TASK-009 (2026-06-23)**, wired as a plugin-level `SessionStart` hook. Plugin-level hook paths DO expand `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, so the healer itself never goes stale.
- **`--apply-settings` does NOT repair a stale entry** — reproduced empirically: it printed `already up-to-date (no write needed)` against a fully stale file, because `mergeContextMonitorSettings`'s presence checks match the *stale* entry and skip the append. My recommended fix would not have worked.

Correcting a coordinator's stated premise before implementing it is the behaviour I want; recording it here so the correction outlives the conversation.

## What the review then found — the answer to the human's actual question

I asked the reviewer not to accept "it already works" without exercising it. It didn't, and the answer explains six weeks of recurrence:

**`repin.mjs` repaired the statusline and was structurally blind to the canonical nested hook shape.** It walked only `hooks[event][i].command` — the flat form — and skipped every nested entry at its `typeof entry.command !== 'string'` early return. Reproduced verbatim: statusline repaired, `Stop[0].hooks[0].command` untouched.

**That is exactly the reported symptom**: the status bar comes back after a restart, the context-monitor hooks stay dead, nothing says so.

And round 1 made it *worse* — its new message asserted "the statusline **and context-monitor hooks** are now re-pointed … No action needed." **A false all-clear is a stronger failure mode than the silence it replaced.**

**Live corroboration, found incidentally:** the reviewer invoked the **installed 0.18.0** copy and watched it repair only `statusLine` and print nothing — direct evidence that the pre-fix code is what the human has been running.

## The design worth keeping

The obvious way to answer "is everything current now?" is to derive it from what the repair pass did — which makes the check **blind in exactly the same way the repair is**, re-shipping the false all-clear one level down.

Instead `allCurrent` comes from `countStaleContextMonitorCommandsDeep`, a **structurally independent re-scan** of the whole post-repair object at any depth under any key. The reviewer planted five shapes the repair cannot reach — an arbitrary key, a non-array `hooks`, a doubly-nested chain, a hybrid entry, an unparseable path — and `allCurrent` returned `false` for **every one**, including failing *closed* on the unparseable case. **This design would have caught the HIGH that caused the round.**

The reviewer also answered the question honestly rather than flatteringly: the two halves **do** share exactly one axis — both gate on `isContextMonitorCommand`, so they are traversal-independent but **predicate-coupled**. A stale command naming a context-monitor script outside the four-name regex yields a false "No action needed." Unreachable today, and the fix is to match a `context-monitor/` path segment instead of filenames. Carried forward, not blocking.

## Also fixed

The documented manual command **did not run** — `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is set only for plugin hook subprocesses, not a user shell, so the doc's block failed with `Cannot find module 'C:\Program Files\Git\context-monitor\repin.mjs'`. It now resolves `installPath` from `installed_plugins.json` first; the reviewer ran both steps verbatim in a plain shell and confirmed exit 0. The doc also now names the broken form explicitly, since that string is findable in the wild.

`repin.mjs` now traverses **both** shapes for path repair only — never converting one to the other. Legacy flat entries exist on disk in every project initialized to date and still need re-pointing; a nested-only fix would have stranded exactly the population that needs it most.

## The seam with TASK-210

This ticket fixes **path staleness**. It does not establish that the shape on disk is one Claude Code will execute — that is TASK-210's writer/schema defect, confirmed separately by `claude doctor` rejecting the flat form outright. `repin.mjs`'s header now **explicitly retracts** its own earlier AC4 claim rather than leaving it to be discovered: *"do not read the original claim as still accurate on its own — it was conditional on this script actually repairing everything, which HIGH-1 disproved."*

The two fixes compose deliberately: repin owns paths across both shapes, TASK-210 owns shape migration. Neither is sufficient alone.

## Carried forward (none blocking)

The predicate coupling above; a hybrid entry carrying both `hooks[]` and a flat `command` repairs only the nested side (`allCurrent` still catches it); **`src/claude-settings.js:13-31` still carries the superseded AC4 rationale** — relayed to TASK-210, which owns that file; a doc clause noting `installPath` changes every update so step 1 must be re-run rather than the expanded command saved; and `tests/context-monitor-repin-fixround.spec.js` uses a computed dynamic import (TASK-109 class), so `test:changed` selects zero specs for a `repin.mjs`-only change.

**Deferral accepted:** mixed path separators in the rewritten command — the substring splice is the conservative algorithm, `C:\a\b/c.mjs` resolves correctly on Windows, and swapping in real path manipulation under active sibling concurrency was the worse trade.
